title: PeFAD: A Parameter-Efficient Federated Framework for Time Series Anomaly Detection

problem.claim: Time series anomaly detection identifies deviant samples from the normal sample distribution and is practically important for data generated by mobile sensing applications.

gap.claim: Existing anomaly detection approaches generally assume centrally available time series, while edge-device deployments increasingly collect data in a decentralized manner.

contributions.claim: PeFAD is a parameter-efficient federated anomaly detection framework for decentralized time series data under increasing privacy concerns.

The framework uses a pre-trained language model as the body of each client's local model and fine-tunes and communicates only small-scale parameters to reduce communication overhead and local adaptation cost.

PeFAD combines an anomaly-driven mask selection strategy with knowledge distillation on a shared synthetic privacy-preserving dataset to address neglected anomalies during training and cross-client data heterogeneity.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly state that PeFAD is the first framework to employ a pre-trained language model as the body of the client's local model for this setting.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive evaluations on four real datasets.
The authors report that PeFAD outperforms existing state-of-the-art baselines by up to 28.74%.

narrative_sequence.summary: Mobile sensing generates large amounts of time series data, making anomaly detection practically important.
Centralized assumptions in existing approaches do not match increasingly decentralized edge-device data collection.
PeFAD is proposed as a parameter-efficient federated framework intended to connect decentralized data with centralized anomaly detection while addressing privacy concerns.
The framework uses a pre-trained language model, parameter-efficient federated training, anomaly-driven mask selection, and knowledge distillation on shared synthetic data.
The authors report evaluation on four real datasets and improvements of up to 28.74% over existing state-of-the-art baselines.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the four datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or experimental protocol.
The abstract does not quantify communication overhead, local adaptation cost, or privacy guarantees.
The abstract does not describe the pre-trained language model, mask-selection procedure, or distillation algorithm in implementation detail.
